title: Generic injection and evasion indicators
note: Strings that are harmless on their own but suspicious in combination. Rules with classification `indicator` are scored together per file: a finding is only reported when the summed weight reaches 30, and these families are never reported as confirmed.

defaults.falsePositives: Each string has legitimate uses; only combinations are reported, and never as proof.
defaults.limitations: Packed or encrypted binaries hide their imports; absence of these strings proves nothing.

rules.name: Remote thread creation API
rules.description: The binary imports CreateRemoteThread, the classic API for running code inside another process.

rules.name: Remote memory allocation API
rules.description: The binary imports VirtualAllocEx, used to allocate memory inside another process.

rules.name: Remote memory write API
rules.description: The binary imports WriteProcessMemory, used to write code or data into another process.

rules.name: Undocumented thread creation API
rules.description: The binary references NtCreateThreadEx, an undocumented API used by injectors to bypass CreateRemoteThread monitoring.

rules.name: Attach to running Java VM from native code
rules.description: The binary calls JNI_GetCreatedJavaVMs, which native code injected into javaw.exe uses to obtain the game's JVM and load cheat classes into it.

rules.name: JVM tool interface agent entry point
rules.description: The binary exports Agent_OnAttach, the entry point of a native JVMTI agent that can be attached to a running game.

rules.name: Runtime class redefinition
rules.description: Compiled classes call Instrumentation.redefineClasses, which rewrites already loaded game classes at runtime.

rules.name: Instrumentation API usage
rules.description: Compiled classes use the java.lang.instrument API, which Java agents use to transform game classes.

rules.name: Dynamic agent attach API
rules.description: Compiled classes use the Attach API to load an agent into a running JVM — the mechanism of Java-based injectors.

rules.name: Global input hook library (JNativeHook)
rules.description: The archive bundles JNativeHook, which gives Java programs global mouse and keyboard hooks and is the basis of most Java auto-clickers.
rules.falsePositives: Hotkey and overlay mods also use global hooks.

rules.name: Synthetic mouse input from Java
rules.description: Compiled classes use java.awt.Robot, which generates synthetic mouse clicks and key presses.

rules.name: Mixin (SpongePowered)
rules.description: The Mixin framework ships an optional Java agent (org.spongepowered.tools.agent) that uses instrumentation for hot-swapping during development. Its classes are exempt from indicator scoring.

rules.name: Byte Buddy
rules.description: Byte Buddy is a code-generation library with an agent installer. Its classes are exempt from indicator scoring.

rules.name: Kotlin coroutines debug agent
rules.description: The kotlinx.coroutines debug agent uses instrumentation. Its classes are exempt from indicator scoring.

rules.name: Fabric Loader
rules.description: Fabric Loader's own classes are exempt from indicator scoring.

rules.name: ObjectWeb ASM
rules.description: The ASM bytecode library is exempt from indicator scoring.

rules.name: Spark profiler
rules.description: The spark profiler attaches profiling agents. Its classes are exempt from indicator scoring.

rules.name: Allatori obfuscator watermark
rules.description: The archive was processed with the demo edition of the Allatori obfuscator, which leaves this watermark in encrypted string constants. Paid cheat clients are commonly obfuscated.
rules.falsePositives: Some legitimate closed-source mods are obfuscated.

rules.name: Java agent in a script or configuration
rules.description: A script or configuration file inside the instance passes -javaagent to Java, i.e. it starts Java with an instrumentation agent that can rewrite game classes.
rules.falsePositives: Launcher configuration files that legitimately configure a profiler or the launcher's own agent.
